title: Around town, shopping, time
goal: Ask where things are and how to get there, ask prices and bargain, and talk about times and days.

notes.h: Where is it? How do I get there?
notes.p: Say the place first, then ask. {{喺邊度呀？|hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3}} = where is it, and {{點去呀？|dim2 heoi3 aa3}} = how do I get there. Directions put the verb first: {{轉左|zyun3 zo2}} turn left, {{轉右|zyun3 jau6}} turn right, {{一直行|jat1 zik6 haang4}} go straight. Where something is uses {{喺|hai2}} (at), not {{係|hai6}} (is).
ex: dei6 tit3 zaam6 dim2 heoi3 aa3
How do I get to the MTR station?
sai2 sau2 gaan1 hai2 zo2 bin6
The restroom is on the left.

notes.p: Say the word, then {{唔|m4}}, then the word again: {{遠唔遠|jyun5 m4 jyun5}} = far or not far? With {{有|jau5}} the question is {{有冇|jau5 mou5}}. Answer by repeating the word: {{遠|jyun5}} or {{唔遠|m4 jyun5}}.

In {{幾多錢呀？|gei2 do1 cin2 aa3}} the word for money rises to cin2. Prices in speech are a number + {{蚊|man1}} (dollars). Two dollars is {{兩蚊|loeng5 man1}}, but twenty is {{二十蚊|ji6 sap6 man1}}. {{太|taai3}} + word + {{喇|laa3}} = "too …!", and word + {{啲|di1}} = "a bit more …". Careful: {{買|maai5}} buy rises, {{賣|maai6}} sell is low and flat.
ex: peng4 di1 dak1 m4 dak1 aa3
Can you make it a bit cheaper?

notes.p: {{點|dim2}} after a number = o'clock, and {{半|bun3}} = half past. Two o'clock is {{兩點|loeng5 dim2}}, never {{二點|ji6 dim2}}. Time words go before the verb, either before or after the person: {{我聽日去|ngo5 ting1 jat6 heoi3}} or {{聽日我去|ting1 jat6 ngo5 heoi3}}.

{{星期|sing1 kei4}} + a number: Monday is {{星期一|sing1 kei4 jat1}}, Saturday {{星期六|sing1 kei4 luk6}}. Sunday is not "week seven" but {{星期日|sing1 kei4 jat6}}, with a low jat6 (sun/day), not the high jat1 of one. You'll also hear {{禮拜|lai5 baai3}} in place of {{星期|sing1 kei4}}.

t: sai2 sau2 gaan1 hai2 bin1 dou6 aa3

vocab.note: In speech 邊 here is usually bin6. You will also hear zo2 bin1; both are correct.
Also heard as jau6 bin1; both are correct.

vocab.note: 吓 (haa5) after a verb = "briefly, a bit".
Number + {{蚊|man1}}: {{十蚊|sap6 man1}} = ten dollars, {{兩蚊|loeng5 man1}} = two dollars.
{{星期|sing1 kei4}} = week; add the number. You'll also hear {{禮拜一|lai5 baai3 jat1}}.
Not "week seven". The last syllable is a low jat6. Also {{禮拜日|lai5 baai3 jat6}}.

roleplay.title: Bargaining at a street market
roleplay.setup: You're at a street market in Mong Kok looking at a T-shirt. Ask the price, bargain a little, and find out if you can pay by card.
roleplay.persona: You are a cheerful stall owner at a street market in Mong Kok. T-shirts are 120 dollars each; if the customer bargains you go down to 100, and you'll do two for 180. You only take cash, no cards. Say prices the spoken way (number + man1). Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-4, in short sentences.
opening: nei5 hou2! soeng2 maai5 me1 aa3
roleplay.opening_en: Hi! What would you like to buy?

roleplay.title: Finding your way
roleplay.setup: You're lost on a street in Tsim Sha Tsui. Ask a passer-by where the MTR station is, whether it's far, and what time it is.
roleplay.persona: You are Mrs Wong, a friendly local woman in her fifties. The MTR station is close: go straight, then turn left; it's about five minutes' walk, on the right. The time now is half past three. Speak simple colloquial Hong Kong Cantonese using mostly words from levels 1-4, in short sentences, and repeat slowly if asked.
opening: jau5 me1 ho2 ji5 bong1 nei5 aa3
goals: Ask where the MTR station is or how to get there
